children: has discontinued the development of VHB937/lifonebart, an experimental therapy for a fatal nervous system disease known as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, following a mid-stage trial failure.

In a community update shared with the European Organization for Professionals and People with ALS, the Swiss drugmaker said it is ending R&D work on VHB937 after its ASTRALS Phase 2 clinical trial didn’t meet its primary or secondary endpoints.

“While these results are not what we had hoped for, we remain committed to advancing scientific understanding of neurodegenerative diseases and applying the learnings from this study to future research efforts,” Novartis
stated in the statement posted on August 25.
Endpoints News first reported the setback on Tuesday, the latest in a series of study failures Novartis
Close on the heels of a late-stage trial failure for a heart disease therapy it developed with Ionis Pharmaceuticals
, the company announced a Phase 3 trial setback for its RNA-based therapy del-desiran in a rare muscle-wasting disease called myotonic dystrophy

title: Novartis scraps ALS therapy after mid-stage trial setback
